_doc: KCC framework definitions used by db.seed.load_seed.
This replaces the legacy prototype seed dependency and intentionally
contains only framework metadata, not demo agents, assays, or evidence.

kccs.title: Electrophilicity & metabolic activation
kccs.description: Is electrophilic or can be metabolically activated to electrophiles that form covalent adducts with macromolecules.
kccs.mechanism: Compounds undergo phase-I metabolic activation, often via CYP450, to produce reactive intermediates that covalently bind nucleophilic sites in DNA, RNA, and proteins.

kccs.title: Genotoxicity
kccs.description: Induces DNA damage including strand breaks, mutations, micronuclei, chromosomal aberrations, or DNA-protein crosslinks.
kccs.mechanism: Direct or indirect induction of DNA lesions detectable in standardized genotoxicity batteries; high concordance with carcinogenicity in long-term rodent bioassays.

kccs.title: Altered DNA repair / genomic instability
kccs.description: Alters DNA repair capacity or causes large-scale genomic instability, such as aneuploidy, polyploidy, or chromothripsis.
kccs.mechanism: Indirect carcinogens may not damage DNA themselves but compromise repair fidelity or chromosomal segregation, amplifying mutational burden over time.

kccs.title: Epigenetic alterations
kccs.description: Induces changes in DNA methylation, histone modification, or non-coding RNA expression that persist across cell divisions.
kccs.mechanism: Heritable changes in gene expression without alteration of DNA sequence can silence tumor suppressors or activate oncogenes long after exposure.

kccs.title: Oxidative stress
kccs.description: Induces oxidative stress via ROS/RNS, mitochondrial dysfunction, or depletion of antioxidant defenses.
kccs.mechanism: Excess reactive species cause oxidative DNA lesions, lipid peroxidation, and signaling dysregulation; chronic ROS exposure is mechanistically linked to multiple tumor types.

kccs.title: Chronic inflammation
kccs.description: Induces or sustains chronic inflammation through cytokine release, immune cell recruitment, or persistent tissue injury.
kccs.mechanism: Sustained inflammatory microenvironments produce ROS/RNS, growth factors, and immunosuppressive signals that promote initiation, promotion, and progression.

kccs.title: Immunosuppression
kccs.description: Is immunosuppressive and decreases immune surveillance against transformed cells.
kccs.mechanism: Reduced immune surveillance permits clonal expansion of pre-neoplastic cells; particularly relevant for virally driven and skin malignancies.

kccs.title: Receptor-mediated effects
kccs.description: Modulates nuclear receptors or membrane receptors in ways that drive proliferation or differentiation.
kccs.mechanism: Ligand-receptor interactions produce sustained transcriptional reprogramming; especially important for hormone-dependent tissues.

kccs.title: Immortalization
kccs.description: Causes immortalization via telomerase activation or bypass of replicative senescence.
kccs.mechanism: Activation of telomere-maintenance pathways or inactivation of the p53/Rb axis enables indefinite proliferative capacity, a hallmark of malignancy.

kccs.title: Altered proliferation, death & nutrient supply
kccs.description: Alters cell proliferation, cell death, angiogenesis, or nutrient supply in the tissue microenvironment.
kccs.mechanism: Imbalance between proliferation and apoptosis, coupled with neovascularization and metabolic rewiring, supports tumor outgrowth and expansion.

kccs.title: Microbiome alteration
kccs.description: Alters composition or function of the host microbiota in ways linked to carcinogenesis.
kccs.mechanism: Dysbiosis can promote local inflammation, generate genotoxic metabolites, and modulate xenobiotic metabolism.

kccs.title: Cellular senescence
kccs.description: Induces premature cellular senescence and a pro-tumorigenic senescence-associated secretory phenotype.
kccs.mechanism: Senescent cells secrete a pro-inflammatory, pro-mitogenic milieu that can paradoxically promote proliferation and invasion of neighboring cells.

kccs.title: Altered stem-cell dynamics
kccs.description: Disrupts normal stem- or progenitor-cell behavior, including self-renewal, lineage commitment, or niche signaling.
kccs.mechanism: Expansion or mis-differentiation of tissue stem cells generates a larger pool of long-lived cells susceptible to mutation accumulation.

kccs.title: Disrupted intercellular communication
kccs.description: Disrupts gap-junction intercellular communication or other tissue-level signaling.
kccs.mechanism: Loss of gap-junction intercellular communication removes a key homeostatic constraint, allowing initiated cells to escape growth control imposed by neighboring normal cells.
